prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of a tiled walkway bordered by a low wall on the left and a railing on the right, with the camera wearer's own hands and an umbrella shaft in frame 2 appearing brightest at 0.2–0.4 m and the floor receding to 1.5–2.5 m below. A person in a dark blue fuzzy sweater with a backpack moves from the lower-left foreground (0.3–0.5 m) in frames 1–2 to the right foreground (0.4–0.6 m) in frames 3–5, while another person in a green jacket stands 1.0–1.5 m ahead in frames 1–2 and a person in a bright blue hoodie enters on the left at 1.0–1.5 m in frame 3 before crouching to the floor at 0.8–1.2 m in frames 4–5, with three standing figures behind them at 1.8–2.5 m. Across the frames, the sweater wearer's outstretched left arm (reaching within 0.3 m of the green-jacketed person's hands and scissors in frames 1–2) and the camera wearer's own hands (within arm's reach at 0.3 m in frames 2–3) create foreground occlusions over the mid-ground figures and walkway. Compared to RGB alone, the continuous intensity gradient clearly separates the overlapping depth layers of the camera wearer's hands, the umbrella shaft, the sweater wearer's torso, and the crouching blue-hooded figure below. However, the map is unreliable in frame 2 where the green-jacketed person in the upper right is rendered almost black as if far away compared to the bright umbrella shaft, and in frame 4 where the right-side backpack and sweater saturate to pure white while losing surface detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete person instances and worn accessories across the walkway scene, separating the camera wearer's lower-center hands (0.2–0.4 m away in frames 2–3) from the surrounding group stationed between 0.4 m and 2.5 m away. In frames 1–2, the foreground person in the dark blue sweater on the left (0.3–0.5 m) extends an arm to touch the hands of the person in the green jacket (1.0–1.5 m ahead, facing the sweater wearer), with the umbrella shaft in frame 2 splitting the scene and partially occluding the green-jacketed person. In frames 3–5, as the camera turns left and downward, the sweater wearer shifts to the right edge (0.4–0.6 m, facing left/downward away from the camera), a person in a bright blue hoodie moves from standing on the left (1.0–1.5 m) to crouching near the floor (0.8–1.2 m, facing right toward a dropped wristband within their arm's reach), and three partial lower-body figures stand behind them at 1.8–2.5 m along the upper edge. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to count the partially visible people cropped at the top and bottom edges (such as the distant legs at the top of frames 3–5 and the camera wearer's hands at the bottom) as distinct entities. However, it is unreliable where it omits the umbrella in frame 2, misses the scissors and wristbands, merges the sweater wearer's backpack into the person mask in frames 3 and 5 (only labeling it in frame 4), and misclassifies the strap held by the camera wearer's hand in frame 3 as a cell phone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is sparse, detecting only a few 2D body and hand keypoints across the five frames while missing most of the people and limbs visible in the RGB strip. In frame 1, a compact yellow torso skeleton and a dense magenta hand cluster at the upper left locate the green-jacketed person at 1.0–1.5 m facing downward toward the interlocking hands and scissors (within arm's reach of both them and the unmapped foreground sweater wearer at 0.3–0.5 m). In frame 2, a single tilted yellow torso rectangle at the lower left marks the person in the dark blue sweater (0.4 m away, facing right in profile under the occluding umbrella), and in frame 3, a larger yellow torso polygon with head keypoints at the top right tracks that same person (now 0.5 m away on the right, facing left/forward). In frame 4 no skeletons are detected at all despite five people being partially visible, and in frame 5 only a single magenta hand cluster appears in the lower-central foreground (about 1.0 m away) where the crouching blue-hooded person's right hand reaches the floor near the camera wearer's lower hand. While the detected magenta clusters pinpoint exact multi-joint finger configurations during fine hand interactions in frames 1 and 5 that are small in RGB, the map is largely unreliable due to severe steep-angle and occlusion dropouts that omit all background figures, the crouching person's body, and the camera wearer's own hands.
